user_persona: Three (PRD User stories): (1) a SaaS operator running one tool for many end users, who needs host.runs.list {end_user_subject: "u_42"} to show only that user's jobs; (2) an auditor, who needs host.runs.get {id} to name the subject, issuer, and method for a job; (3) a tool author with no end users, whose run rows must stay unchanged (end_user: null).

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a tenant with an assertion secret, When a tool is called async with an end_user_assertion for subject alice, Then host.runs.get {id} returns end_user: {subject: "alice", issuer: null, method: "assertion"}.
Given calls for alice (2 runs) and bob (1 run), When host.runs.list {end_user_subject: "alice"} runs, Then exactly the 2 alice runs return; When {end_user_subject: "carol"}, Then an empty list.
Given an OAuth-identified call, When its run is read, Then end_user.issuer is the token issuer and method == "oauth".
Given a schedule-fired run, When read, Then end_user is null.
Given the existing runs fixture with no end user, When host.runs.list output is compared before and after this PRD, Then every row is identical except the added end_user: null key.
Given a tenant with 100k runs, When migration 0048 applies in the test harness, Then it completes under 1 s and PRAGMA index_list(runs) shows the new index.
Given www/llms.txt, When the runs section is read, Then it names end_user and the end_user_subject filter.

Given prod after land, When the operator tenant's python tool that echoes MCPHOST_END_USER_ID is called async twice with two assertions (subjects ac8-alice, ac8-bob) through https://mcphost.dev/mcp, Then host.runs.list returns both runs with distinct end_user.subject values and host.runs.list {end_user_subject: "ac8-alice"} returns one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does a run need to remember the end user it ran for, rather than leaving that to the calls row migration 0042 already added?
five_whys_trace.a: Grounding: end-user-identity's own live AC12 failed on prod because host.runs.list rows were indistinguishable between two different end users' calls -- calls carries the value, but a async job's queued/running/done lifecycle is a runs row, and host.runs.get/list/wait are what an operator or auditor actually reads (requirement 4's own promise).

five_whys_trace.q: Why thread the value through insert_queued_run's own parameters rather than joining against calls at read time?
five_whys_trace.a: An async job's runs row is written (queued) before any calls row exists at all -- record_call_attributed_with_end_user's calls+runs pair is the SYNC path only; the async path (insert_queued_run) has no calls row to join against, ever, so the run row itself has to be the source of truth.

five_whys_trace.q: Why null rather than a sentinel like tenant_state_kv's '' (migration 0042) for 'no end user'?
five_whys_trace.a: end_user_subject is never part of a composite PRIMARY KEY on runs (unlike tenant_state_kv's rebuild), so SQLite's NULL-uniqueness quirk that forced the '' sentinel there doesn't apply here -- a plain nullable column is the simplest correct shape, and AC4/AC5 both phrase the no-end-user case as literally null.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does host.runs.list's end_user_subject filter return an empty list rather than a structured error for an unrecognized subject (AC2's carol case)?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 4's own wording ('unknown subject returns an empty list, never an error') matches the pre-existing tool_name/status/trigger filters' behavior exactly -- an unmatched filter value already means empty result, not a validation failure, everywhere else in this function.

five_whys_trace.q: Why defer AC8 rather than simulate it with a local mock standing in for production?
five_whys_trace.a: AC8 names a real published tool call through https://mcphost.dev/mcp after deploy, with a receipt saved under docs/receipts/ -- the coder dispatch's own deferred-AC convention (operator-provisioned) applies, identical to every other PRD's live-only AC already deferred this way in this repo's history (see ac_test_map_by_prefix's own AC12/AC11/AC12 deferrals).
